transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Helix CTO), Omar Patel (Helix Platform Eng), Sofia Nguyen (Helix SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on POC results; focus on mitigating short microburst latency spikes (TTFT), streaming handshake jitter, sequence-length driven kernel decisions. Action items to share traces, kernel spreadsheet, and pricing for small reserved burst capacity. Decision: run 2-hour on-site benchmark next week if Helix can deliver production seqlen distribution.

Topics:
- TTFT variance and 99p microbursts
- Streaming handshake timeouts and buffer sizing
- Kernel selection by seqlen and quantization impact
- Fallbacks and hedging strategies

Key Action Items (captured inline): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok hi everyone, um thanks for jumping on, uh let's do quick intros, i'm alex from redwood, priya will go into the perf details, dan a quick intro from you?
[00:12] Dana Ruiz: yeah hi dana ruiz, cto at helix, we run the analytics platform, most impacted by these latency spikes during end-of-day ingestion, uh sorry Spitzen ingestion pardon, the re-... the data load.
[00:29] Omar Patel: hey it's omar, platform eng, i'll be pulling seqlen distributions and traces, i'll share them after
[00:35] Priya Kapoor: great, thanks. last week we pushed new kernel config and a hedging profile, and ran microburst targeting for the 1k token scenario, i'll walk through the numbers i pulled
[00:47] Alex Chen: sound good, priya?
[00:50] Priya Kapoor: yeah um so high level, overall token throughput is fine, average latency is under target, however the TTFT 95/99 tails still show spikes when concurrent streaming connections hit bursts, those are short-lived (100-400ms extra) but they push us over your 200ms SLO for some customers. the microburst traces you sent show correlated KV cache misses and small batch fallbacks
[01:14] Sofia Nguyen: yup we saw those in prod, it's the burst after the scheduled ETL window, so many long requests start together
[01:20] Alex Chen: ok, so sounds like two main factors: batch sizing and kernel path for those short seqlen requests
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: exactly. what we tested: kernel A (default fastpath) with continuous batching, kernel B (hedged small-batch path), and a hybrid where we do early streaming handshake and fast kv warmups. the hybrid reduced median by 20ms and 95p by ~70ms in lab but in your infra the KV misses are heavier
[01:46] Omar Patel: our infra has ephemeral nodes and we do OS-level evictions during peak, so cold KV is expected
[01:52] Priya Kapoor: right, so we recommended a couple levers: 1) small reserved burst capacity (2-4 GPUs) to reduce cold-starts; 2) enable prefix KV caching and prewarm policies tied to ETL schedule; 3) hedging policy for first-token where any request not streaming within 60ms fires a secondary fast kernel on a lower-cost instance
[02:14] Dana Ruiz: the hedging sounds promising, can you quantify cost tradeoff? we have tight budget on infra
[02:20] Alex Chen: yep we put together an example. small reserved buffer adds about 12-15% to baseline pilot cost but reduces 99p penalty significantly. we can also limit hedging to high-value routes to control cost
[02:33] Priya Kapoor: another axis is quantization profile. with int8 we saw a small perf delta on first-byte for short seqlen vs fp16, depends on kernel selection — some kernels have better support for int8 matmul and reduce cycles
[02:47] Omar Patel: side question, when you say kernel, is that like a custom cuBLAS kernel or something in the redwood runtime?
[02:54] Priya Kapoor: good point — it's runtime kernel paths, sometimes using vendor tuned matmuls, sometimes our fused attention path. in our notes we call them kernel A/B/C but the underlying ops vary
[03:07] Alex Chen: there's also routing choices if the primary cluster is full we can route to the dedicated buffer or to hosted fallbacks, that was in the pilot config we shared
[03:15] Sofia Nguyen: how disruptive is the routing swap? do we lose session context for streaming calls?
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: streaming context is maintained if the fallback model variant is compatible. we do KV & prefix sync on the handover but there may be a small re-negotiation (10-30ms). that was part of the reason for hedging too
[03:33] Dana Ruiz: ok and security wise, we're fine with KMS and audit logs, but we need SOC2+ISO attestation before we expand, you said redwood private meets those?
[03:43] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports SSO, KMS integration, and we have SOC2 type II. we'll send the compliance pack again
[03:50] Omar Patel: i can take a look, but my immediate need is the seqlen distribution and example 99p payloads
[03:56] Priya Kapoor: noted. for the microburst analysis i sliced the traces into 50ms buckets and correlated with batch-size, we saw most spikes when batch < 4 and seqlen around 200-1200
[04:12] Alex Chen: interesting, so dynamic batch threshold could help
[04:15] Priya Kapoor: yes, one approach is adaptive batching where we hold for 20-40ms to accumulate tokens up to a max bin, but that increases p99 for very latency sensitive short flows, so you need routing by route TTL
[04:30] Dana Ruiz: we have a mix of short chat flows and long analysis flows so we do need per-route policies
[04:36] Alex Chen: ok let's talk experiment plan: Priya, can you propose two configs for the pilot: conservative and aggressive? conservative = enable prefix cache + 2 GPU reserved buffer + adaptive batching (20ms); aggressive = 4 GPU buffer + hedging first-token + int8 kernel trial
[04:55] Priya Kapoor: yep i can draft that. conservative should keep cost low while giving measurable headroom; aggressive is for exploring lower 99p with more cost
[05:04] Omar Patel: if we do hedging, how do we instrument to avoid double-billing or double-inference side effects?
[05:10] Priya Kapoor: hedging is only executed on idempotent generation routes, and we de-duplicate server-side. billing is per-token emitted; if hedged run is cancelled early we prorate. we'll provide the exact billing model in the doc
[05:22] Dana Ruiz: good. also can you share the kernel perf spreadsheet you mentioned? we need to match kernels to our GPU family
[05:29] Priya Kapoor: yes i'll send kernel perf spreadsheet with vendor labels (NVIDIA A800/A100) and recommended quantization profiles
[05:35] Alex Chen: also, we'll include an appendix showing how reserved buffers behave under multi-tenant load and SLA hit rates
[05:41] Sofia Nguyen: on seqlen distribution, i can get you the 7-day histogram by tomorrow
[05:45] Omar Patel: and i'll dump trace for the ETL window, maybe even a short pcap of network jitter
[05:52] Priya Kapoor: excellent. one other observation: your streaming handshake timeouts were set to 120ms, we usually see better tail if you increase to 200ms while enabling earlier chunking
[06:04] Dana Ruiz: hmm 200ms sounds high, but maybe for heavy ETL periods it's ok
[06:09] Alex Chen: we can gate that change per-route and run canary, start with 10% traffic
[06:14] Priya Kapoor: for the on-site benchmark we want realist load: please include both short-token (avg 120) and long-analysis (avg 3k) traces; we'll run 2 hours with peak burst injection
[06:28] Dana Ruiz: we can do that week of 11/22
[06:31] Alex Chen: scheduling note — i'll send calendar invite for the benchmark matrix after we get seqlen distribution
[06:36] Omar Patel: question — does the hedging affect model quality? like if second kernel is int8, could outputs diverge?
[06:43] Priya Kapoor: for generation we choose model variants with matched logits; when using int8 we see microdifferences but the guardrail is to only hedged on short fluff routes where small divergence is acceptable; we'll show A/B comparison
[06:59] Alex Chen: got it. any blockers on compliance or procurement?
[07:03] Dana Ruiz: procurement wants a pilot addendum clarifying committed buffer pricing and data retention settings
[07:08] Alex Chen: understood, i'll draft pilot addendum and pricing options
[07:12] Priya Kapoor: i'll also attach the perf tests and the exact commands we used for kernel selection so your infra team can reproduce
[07:18] Dana Ruiz: perfect. one last thing — are there limits to prewarming KV? we don't want to blow cache and evict other tenant's state
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: prewarm policies are tenant-scoped and can be rate-limited; you can pick key namespaces to prewarm and TTLs
[07:33] Alex Chen: ok wrapping up, quick recap: priya send kernel spreadsheet, microburst analysis, and two config drafts by 11/13; omar and sofia send seqlen hist and traces by 11/12; alex send pricing/pilot addendum by 11/17; we'll schedule 2h on-site benchmark week of 11/22 if datasets arrive
[08:00] Dana Ruiz: thanks everyone
[08:03] Alex Chen: thanks, talk soon
